activities.caption: drop the marker — where half the air runs out
activities.name: wxMassPlace

config.prompt: Half the atmosphere's mass lies below what altitude?
config.why: About 5.5 km — Everest's summit pokes above half the air, and pressure keeps halving roughly every 5.5 km above that.

activities.caption: pair each lift mechanism with its weather
activities.name: wxLiftMatch

config.prompt: Pair each lifting mechanism with the weather it makes:

pairs.right: sun-heated ground bubbles air upward — afternoon thunderstorms
windward side wet, rain-shadow side bone dry
warm air riding over a cold wedge — the mid-latitude rain machine
compresses, warms, dries — the physics inside every desert

config.why: Rain's mechanism is rising air; every desert is the signature of its absence.

activities.anchor: Meteorologists compute this comparison from every radiosonde
activities.caption: bet before you read on — the stability verdict
activities.name: wxStabPredict

config.q: A radiosonde shows the surroundings cooling at 7 °C/km while a saturated parcel cools at 5 °C/km. What happens to the parcel?
choices: It stays warmer than its surroundings and keeps rising on its own buoyancy
It turns colder and denser than its environment and sinks back
It hovers at whatever altitude it reaches
config.why: The surroundings cool faster than the parcel, so the parcel stays warmer than its environment — instability, and the atmosphere dumps its energy in towering cumulonimbus.

activities.anchor: Zoom out and the atmosphere runs a heat engine
activities.caption: rebuild the Hadley cell's journey
activities.name: wxHadleyOrder

config.prompt: Rebuild the Hadley cell — follow the air:
items: Intense equatorial heating drives deep convection — air rises (low pressure, daily downpours)
The air flows poleward aloft, cooling as it goes
It sinks near 30° latitude — high pressure, the world's great deserts
Surface flow returns equatorward as the trade winds, closing the cell
config.why: The Sahara, the Outback and the Atacama all sit under the subsiding branch — one cell, both the rain belt and the desert belt.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — reading the weather map
activities.name: wxMapCloze

config.text: The map rules: low pressure means %%0%% air, cloud and rain; high pressure means %%1%% air and clear skies; and tight isobars mean a strong pressure %%2%% — and therefore %%3%%.
config.hint: One rises into cloud, one sinks into clear skies, and the crowd of isobars decides what you feel on your face.

activities.anchor: Lewis Fry Richardson imagined the scheme in 1922
activities.caption: call the cost of the first hand-made forecast
activities.name: wxRichardEst

config.prompt: Richardson's 1922 hand calculation produced one six-hour forecast. How long did the calculation take him?
config.why: Six weeks for one six-hour forecast (and it was wrong) — operational forecasting waited for the first computers in the 1950s.
config.context: today's supercomputers run the same equations for the whole globe in minutes

activities.caption: with and without the blanket — drag the divider
activities.name: wxGreenCompare

config.prompt: The greenhouse effect's service — drag the divider:

before.label: without it
before.text: the surface averages −18 °C and the oceans freeze

after.label: with it
after.text: +15 °C — a 33 °C blanket from water vapour, CO₂ and methane re-emitting infrared back down

config.why: Not a hypothesis but measured spectroscopy — the question is only how much of the blanket we are adding.

activities.anchor: What distinguishes the present change is the fingerprint
activities.caption: find the backwards claim — the fingerprint test
activities.name: wxFingerSpot

config.prompt: One of these climate-fingerprint claims is backwards — click it:
lines: Ice cores preserve ancient air in bubbles and ancient temperatures in isotopes.
A hotter sun would warm the stratosphere along with the surface.
Nights warming faster than days is a greenhouse fingerprint.
Attribution science quantifies how much more likely climate change made a specific heatwave.
config.correction: A hotter sun would warm both layers; the observed fingerprint is a warming surface with a cooling stratosphere — the greenhouse signature.
config.why: The fingerprint separates the drivers: what warms the surface while cooling the stratosphere above it is the greenhouse effect, not the sun.
